newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa urged to develop biotech industries.
newsitem.headline: South Africa urged to develop biotech industries.

text.p: South Africa has been urged to pay greater attention to the development of biotechnology industries.

In an article in the latest issue of the University of Cape Town's Trade Monitor, researcher Rosemary Wolson said that biotechnology had received little attention to date and was generally misunderstood.

Although South Africa could not now compete with major world players, it had enough infrastructure to ensure that biotechnology could provide a "source of useful products, employment and foreign exchange for the country in the future."
Wolson said that there were many opportunities for strategic alliances between local and overseas groups, which could encourage foreign investment.

Although research and development was being conducted into biotechnology by local academic centres and some firms, South Africa lagged far behind world leaders in this area and no dedicated biotechnology company was listed on the Johannesburg Stock Echange.

But South Africa had good life science facilities at several universities, enough infrastructure to import and adapt technology successfully as well as cheap sources of power, carbohydrates and technical facilities.
It also had a "vast wealth of genetic resources" and had been ranked as the third most biologically diverse country in the world.

The constraints facing the development of biotechnology industries included the lack of financial incentives, high start-up costs, misconceptions about the risks involved and the lack of a clear government policy on biotechnology.

Wolson said biotechnology had also been neglected because of the apartheid government's emphasis on technology that would contribute to economic self-sufficiency rather than cutting-edge developments.
